title: Fab City Source Review
description: One person's record of having read one source for one real territory. Reviews are files, not a boolean on the entry, because the thing that makes an entry `live` is testimony with a name on it — and testimony has an author, a date, a place, and a list of what was actually checked. Each review lives at reviews/{pillar}/{scale}/{slug}/{date}-{reviewer-slug}.yaml, alongside the entry it is about at data/{pillar}/{scale}/{slug}.yaml. scripts/validate.py resolves that pointer and fails if it dangles.

entry.description: The registry id this review is about: {pillar}/{scale}/{slug}, the same path the entry file lives at under data/ minus the .yaml. Must resolve to an existing entry, and the review file must sit under reviews/{entry}/.

by.description: The name of the person who read it. A person, not a team and not a bot — the point of a review is that somebody can be asked about it afterwards.

org.description: The lab, city, foundation or institution the reviewer did this as. Says whose hands the source passed through, and lets a reader weigh a self-declared review (see `self_declared`).

date.description: ISO date the reading happened. scripts/check_review.py warns past 365 days and fails past 730: a review is evidence about a source at a moment, and sources move.

territory.description: The real place the source was read FOR — a city, region, island, bioregion. Not 'global' and not the source's own coverage claim: the question a review answers is whether this source works for somewhere, and somewhere has a name.

checked.description: What the reviewer actually verified, from a closed list so that reviews are comparable. licence = the terms permit the use this list implies; endpoint = the URL or API answered, with data in it; admin-code = the source's administrative identifiers join to the territory's own; vintage = how old the newest record is, and how often it moves; field-fit = the fields carry the indicator row this entry is filed against. A short list is honest; an unchecked box is not a failure, it is a thing the next reviewer can do.

verdict.description: usable = a node or a city can read this for the named territory as it stands; usable-with-caveats = it works, and `note` says what the reader must know first; unusable = it does not work for this territory, and `note` says why. Only the first two make an entry `live`.

self_declared.description: True when the reviewer's org is also the source's publisher. Not disqualifying — the publisher often knows the licence and the vintage best — but it is a different kind of evidence than an outside reading, and a reader is entitled to see which one this is.

assisted_by.description: The AI agent or tool that did part of the checks, named (e.g. 'Claude Code'). The reviewer is still `by`: the person who read the findings, stands behind the verdict and filed the issue from their own account. Absent means the person did the checks themselves. Like self_declared, it tells a reader which kind of evidence this is.

issue.description: The issue number this review arrived on, when it came through .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/source-review.yml. Absent for a review committed by hand.

note.description: What the reviewer wants the next reader to know: the caveat behind usable-with-caveats, the reason behind unusable, the rate limit, the join that had to be built. Required by nothing and worth more than everything else in the file.
